source_user: Write a concise runbook entry for an engineer investigating quantization. Case variant 4: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Runbook: first record the NCCL version, communicator topology, ranks, GPU mapping, transport selection, message sizes, and timeout policy. Mechanism: a collective such as all-reduce exchanges rank-partitioned data through topology-aware kernels/transports, so each rank must participate consistently. Compare a healthy matched run with traces for collective duration, link traffic, GPU utilization, and errors. Boundary: behavior is not portable across GPU, driver, fabric, topology, or message-size regimes; do not infer a universal speedup without those measurements.
risks: Collective performance and failure behavior depend on rank synchronization, topology, transport, message size, and software versions.
Averages or isolated NCCL microbenchmarks can hide stragglers, timeouts, fallback paths, and end-to-end workload effects.
evidence_required: NCCL/CUDA/driver versions, rank-to-device mapping, topology, transport/algorithm logs, tensor contract, and workload matrix.
Repeated matched measurements with per-rank timing, bandwidth, tails, GPU/link utilization, errors, retries, and timeout accounting.
